description: Held-out data-analysis items over fixed tables.

items.prompt:
```csv
id,region,latency_ms,status
n01,eu-west,104,ok
n02,us-east,111,ok
n03,eu-west,98,ok
n04,ap-south,860,degraded
n05,us-east,107,ok
n06,eu-west,102,ok
```

Identify the anomalous node id(s) whose latency is a clear outlier. Answer with a comma-separated list of ids only.
items.explanation: n04 is ~8σ above the mean of the remaining nodes.

items.prompt:
```csv
id,region,latency_ms,status
n01,eu-west,104,ok
n02,us-east,111,ok
n03,eu-west,98,ok
n04,ap-south,120,degraded
n05,us-east,107,ok
```

Compute the median of `latency_ms` across all rows (2 dp). Answer with the number only.

```csv
throughput,latency
10,180
20,166
30,151
40,133
50,120
60,104
```

Classify the linear relationship between `throughput` and `latency` as POSITIVE, NEGATIVE or NONE (|Pearson r| <= 0.5 counts as NONE).
items.explanation: Latency decreases monotonically with throughput; r ≈ -0.999.

items.prompt:
```csv
miner,tasks,correct
alpha,120,108
bravo,40,38
cirrus,300,240
```

Which miner has the highest accuracy? Answer with the miner name only.
items.explanation: 0.90, 0.95, 0.80 → bravo. Note the sample-size caveat the emission model addresses separately.
